title: Besleme yolu: AVDD → VREF → V_MID
why_now: The voltage signal path is done; it rests on V_MID (zero line) and on AVDD (op-amp supply). This chapter shows where both come from. Path change: announce it with the signal-vs-supply map.
upstream: Arty 3V3 rail (from the Arty's own regulators, fed by the 12 V adapter)
downstream: V_MID feeds the divider bottom and every R_g (voltage block)
AVDD feeds every op-amp and the TL431
VREF_BUF feeds the Ω block (introduced there, not here)
Q1 open-lead test nudges V_MID (own chapter)
review: novice-reader pass 24 Nov 01:15: fixes applied (R1.3 split, every bare number given a source, C1 cut, mid node vs V_MID made explicit, cutoff idea pictured before any 159 Hz)

units.title: AVDD: sakin besleme
units.status: explained 23 Nov, not checked; re-run briefly from the drawing
units.need: The op-amps and the reference need a quiet supply. The Arty's 3V3 carries fast up-and-down wiggles (ripple from its regulator, short spikes when the FPGA switches).

names.AVDD: filtered 3.3 V for the analog chips

units.bridge: map-signal-vs-supply: the supply-path row, box 'AVDD filter'
units.drawing: 3V3 (noisy line) → R6 10 Ω → AVDD node (calm line), C2 100 µF to GND. Second panel: a short spike barely moves AVDD (charge limited by R6), a slow 2 ms step passes. AVDD ≈ 3.23 V because the analog chips draw about 3.7 mA through R6: 3.7 mA × 10 Ω ≈ 37 mV.

check.q: Two changes on 3V3: a 0.03 µs spike and a 5 ms dip. Which one reaches AVDD, and why?
check.a: the 5 ms dip: it lasts long enough for charge to flow through R6 into C2; the spike is over before C2 can change

values.teaching: AVDD ≈ 3.23 V; '159 Hz' only shown as the dividing line, not asked
values.real: 3.09–3.36 V over all boards and loads (revealed in R1.2)

traps: It filters the supply, not the measured signal (23 Nov confusion)
R alone doesn't filter; R and C together
units.claim: A resistor in series with a capacitor to ground smooths the supply: fast changes can't move enough charge through R into C, slow ones can.
rubric: names the slow change (5 ms) as the one that passes
reason mentions charge/current limited by R6 or time for C to fill
does not claim R alone filters

units.title: Neden bir referans gerekiyor?
units.need: V_MID must sit at one known voltage. AVDD itself differs from board to board and with load: 3.09–3.36 V.

names.VREF: a fixed voltage that doesn't follow AVDD

units.bridge: R1.1 drawing; add a divider from AVDD that would give 1.5 V
units.drawing: AVDD → divider with ratio 0.464 (= 1.5 / 3.23, chosen to give 1.5 V from a typical AVDD) → 'V_MID?'. Two boards side by side: AVDD 3.09 V → 1.43 V, AVDD 3.36 V → 1.56 V. Last panel: the same divider fed from a fixed 'VREF' box gives the same V_MID on both boards.

key_question.q: If we made V_MID by dividing AVDD directly (×0.464), what is V_MID on a board with AVDD 3.09 V and on one with 3.36 V?
key_question.a: 1.43 V vs 1.56 V: the zero line differs by 130 mV between boards, and drifts with load

values.real: the real design divides VREF by 0.6 (R1.5)

traps: Don't name TL431 yet; this unit only creates the need
units.claim: Dividing AVDD directly makes V_MID move with AVDD; a fixed reference is needed.
rubric: computes both values (≈1.43 V and ≈1.56 V) or the ≈130 mV difference
concludes that the zero line would differ between boards / drift

units.title: TL431: 2.495 V'u tutan parça
units.need: A part that keeps one voltage, 2.495 V, whatever AVDD does.

names.TL431: a 3-leg part: cathode (top) and REF both on VREF, anode on GND; it holds VREF at 2.495 V
names.R1@supply: the resistor from AVDD to VREF

units.bridge: R1.2 last panel: open the 'VREF' box
units.drawing: Black box first: AVDD → R1 220 Ω → VREF node → TL431 → GND, symbol drawn with its three legs labelled; on the drawing itself: 'R1 here = 220 Ω (not the R1 of our divider lessons)'. Three AVDD values (3.09 / 3.23 / 3.36 V) all give VREF = 2.495 V; only R1's voltage changes.

check.q: AVDD rises from 3.09 V to 3.36 V. Which voltage changes: VREF or the one across R1? By how much?
check.a: across R1: from 0.595 V to 0.865 V (+0.27 V); VREF stays 2.495 V

values.real: VREF 2.467–2.520 V between parts; AVDD moving 270 mV moves VREF < 1 mV

traps: Name clash R1: on the drawing, not only in words
Behaviour only (black box); currents come in R1.4
units.claim: The TL431 holds VREF at 2.495 V; when AVDD changes, only the voltage across R1 changes.
rubric: says the R1 voltage changes, ≈0.595 → 0.865 V (+0.27 V)

units.title: TL431'in akımı
units.need: The TL431 works only if enough current reaches it: its datasheet asks for at least 1 mA. R1 must supply that, plus whatever the circuit draws from VREF.
units.drawing: Step 1: current through R1 = (AVDD − VREF) / 220 Ω, computed on the drawing. Step 2: at the VREF node that current splits: part to the ×0.6 divider (0.1 mA), the rest into the TL431. Step 3: the TL431 takes whatever is left, as long as ≥ 1 mA.

check.q: AVDD = 3.227 V, VREF = 2.495 V, R1 = 220 Ω: current through R1? If the divider below takes 0.1 mA, how much is left for the TL431, and is it ≥ 1 mA?

values.real: TL431 current 2.46–3.98 mA over all tolerances

traps: series-current-same is only level 1: practise the split with the arrows before the check
units.claim: R1's current is (AVDD − VREF)/R1; at the VREF node it splits between the load and the TL431, which needs at least 1 mA.
rubric: ≈3.23 mA left for the TL431 after 0.1 mA

units.title: ×0.6 bölücü: 1.497 V
units.need: 1.5 V from 2.495 V. Why 1.5: every signal swings ±1.35 V around V_MID (the window agreed in the design: it keeps op-amp outputs away from their limits near 0 V and 3.3 V), so V_MID ≈ 1.5 V puts 0.15–2.85 V safely inside 0–3.3 V.

names.R2..R5@supply: the four 10 kΩ of the ×0.6 divider (R4 ∥ R5 = 5 kΩ)
names.mid-node: the divider's middle point, NOT yet V_MID (V_MID is made from it in R1.6)

units.bridge: R1.4 drawing; the 0.1 mA branch becomes the divider
units.drawing: Window bar first: 0–3.3 V with 1.5 ± 1.35 V marked (0.15 and 2.85 V). Then VREF → R2 10 kΩ → mid node 1.497 V → R3 10 kΩ → R4∥R5 5 kΩ → GND. Note on the drawing: 'R2 here ≠ R2 of our lessons'.

check.q: Warm-up: 10 kΩ ∥ 10 kΩ = ? Then: why is the ratio exactly 0.6?

values.real: 1.466–1.529 V; 15 kΩ isn't sold, hence 10k + two 10k in parallel

units.claim: VREF × 15/25 = 0.6 × 2.495 ≈ 1.497 V, centred so ±1.35 V fits inside 0–3.3 V.

units.title: U1A tamponu: V_MID
units.need: Many places hang on V_MID (the voltage divider's bottom and every R_g); together they can pull up to about 63 µA (the design's worst-case sum, mostly the R_g's when a gain stage is overloaded). The mid node sits behind about 6 kΩ (R2 ∥ 15 kΩ), so it would sag.

names.U1: the third MCP6002 (spelled U1 / U1A); U1A turns the mid node into V_MID (U1B: used later, in the Ω block)

units.bridge: R1.5 drawing; hang the V_MID loads directly on the mid node first
units.drawing: Panel 1 (no buffer): mid node seen as 1.497 V behind 6 kΩ (Thevenin, as in his own derivation); 63 µA × 6 kΩ ≈ 0.38 V sag. Panel 2: mid node → U1A (+), output wired to − → this output is V_MID, 1.497 V under any load. Label: 'mid node ≠ V_MID; V_MID = U1A output'.

check.q: Without U1A, 63 µA flows out of the mid node (≈ 6 kΩ behind it). How far does it move?

values.real: stage 2a: at most 63 µA on V_MID; tap impedance 6.0 kΩ. C1 100 nF on the mid node exists (noise filter) but is not taught here

traps: TAP vs V_MID confusion (fragile): keep 'mid node', 'V_MID' and 'TAP' visually distinct
units.claim: A loaded 6 kΩ node sags by I × 6 kΩ; the U1A buffer's output, not the mid node, is V_MID.
rubric: says the buffer output is V_MID / mid node ≠ V_MID

chapter_close.achieved: AVDD filter, why a reference, TL431 + R1, its current, ×0.6 divider, U1A buffer → V_MID
deferred: C1 noise filter on the mid node
